blanks.document: Banco Central do Brasil, Demonstracoes Financeiras 2023 (audited annual financial statements), Note 11 'Ouro Monetario' (fl. 33) and accounting-policy Note 2.6 'Ouro Monetario' (fl. 13)
blanks.read: PDF downloaded (3.2 MB) and the full extracted text (332,746 characters) grepped for 'ouro', 'custodi', 'depositad', 'exterior', 'Bank of England', 'Reserve Bank', 'BIS'. Note 11 is three sentences long: it gives cost, fair-value adjustment and balance (R$41,674m at 31.12.2023), says the BCB holds part of the country's international reserves in monetary gold, and attributes the year's change to the international gold price and the real/dollar rate. It names no custodian, no institution and no location, domestic or foreign. Note 2.6 is accounting policy only and states that fair value is taken from the London exchange quotation ('cotacao obtida junto a Bolsa de Londres') - that is a price source, not a storage location, and must not be read as one. The BIS appears throughout the document (Note 6.1 BISIP investment pools, Note 12 BIS shareholding, Note 23 counterparty limits) but never in connection with gold storage.
blanks.note: Vein for next round: the BCB gold note has carried no location field for at least the 2016-2023 statements in this series. A different route would be the BCB's Relatorio de Gestao das Reservas Internacionais or an Acesso a Informacao (LAI) request response, not the financial statements.

blanks.document: National Bank of Ukraine, Consolidated Financial Statements for the year ended 31 December 2024 (audited), accounting-policy section on monetary gold (p. 14), Note 6 'Funds and Deposits in Foreign Currency and Investment Metals' (p. 18) and Note 23 'Analysis of Financial Assets and Liabilities by Geographical Concentration Risk' (pp. 53-54)
blanks.read: PDF downloaded (8.4 MB) and the full extracted text (681,474 characters) grepped for 'gold', 'vault', 'storage', 'custod', 'non-resident bank', 'held with/at/in'. There is no separate note on monetary gold: monetary gold sits on the face of the consolidated statement of financial position and the only narrative is the accounting policy, which defines monetary gold as bullion and coins of not less than 995 fineness belonging to the NBU, and adds that 'Gold in foreign banks generating interest is reported as funds and deposits in foreign currency and investment metals' - foreign banks in the plural and unnamed. Note 6 discloses short-term deposits in gold of UAH 9,951 million at 31.12.2024 (UAH 5,932 million at 31.12.2023) and names no counterparty. Note 23, the only geographical table in the document, covers financial assets only and monetary gold is not a line in it, so the Ukraine / OECD / IMF / Other split cannot be read onto the gold. No custodian, and no statement that the holding is domestic.
blanks.note: Vein for next round: the gold-on-deposit counterparties might be reachable through Note 24 (credit risk) rating bands in an earlier year's statements, but those give ratings rather than names in 2024.

blanks.document: Central Bank of Iceland, Annual Report 2022, financial statements, Note 14 'Gold' (p. 58 of the notes) plus the reserve-management chapter (p. 1150 of extracted text) and Note 39 'Gold price risk' (p. 79)
blanks.read: PDF downloaded (3.4 MB) and the full extracted text (381,289 characters) grepped for 'gold'. Note 14 is a four-line movement table: opening balance ISK 15,211,571 thousand, exchange rate difference ISK 1,314,359 thousand, closing balance ISK 16,525,930 thousand, and 'Gold holdings at the year-end, in ounces 63,797'. It names no custodian and no location. The gold-price-risk note adds only that the Bank owns about 64,000 ounces, 2% of the reserves, and that 'The Bank did not loan gold to other financial institutions during the year'. The reserve-management narrative states that deposits were 49% of reserves and 'the vast majority of them held in central banks' - that sentence is about foreign-currency deposits, not about the gold, and was not read onto the gold. Note 15.1 separately discloses deposits with foreign central banks, again not gold.
blanks.note: Vein for next round: Iceland's gold is widely said in trade press to sit at the Bank of England, but nothing in the audited statements says so and the custodian's side is closed by design. The untried route is the Bank's Rules on Reserve Maintenance, referred to in the reserve-maintenance section, which was not opened.

blanks.document: Centrale Bank van Aruba, Condensed Financial Statements 2025 (audited by Ernst & Young), Note 1 'Gold' (p. 12 per the contents list)
blanks.read: PDF downloaded (1.07 MB) and the full extracted text grepped for 'gold', 'custod', 'vault', 'safekeep', 'bewaar', 'Bank of England', 'Federal Reserve', 'Settlements', 'abroad'. Note 1 gives the valuation basis (monthly market pricing from 1 January 2025, quarterly before that), the price per fine troy ounce, a quantity of 111,294.165 fine troy ounces unchanged year on year, and a two-line movement table. It states no location and names no custodian. The phrase 'the gold holdings at the CBA as of December 31, 2025' is a reference to the Bank's own holdings at a date and was deliberately not read as a storage location. Note 4 'Money in custody' is about third-party funds received in custody by the CBA, not about gold.
blanks.note: Found in the same document and belonging to a different row, not filed here: Note 2.1 'Due from banks and other financial institutions' states the CBA's foreign-currency current accounts are held at De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB), the Bank of England (BOE), the Federal Reserve Bank of New York (FRNY), the Centrale Bank van Curacao en St. Maarten (CBCS) and other financial institutions in the U.S.A., with time deposits at a financial institution in Colombia. That is FX deposits, not gold custody, so it is listed in leads_not_opened rather than filed as a gold custodian.

blanks.document: National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic, Consolidated Financial Statements and independent auditor's report for the year ended 31 December 2024, Note 7 'Monetarnoe zoloto' (Monetary gold, p. 44) and accounting-policy Note 3(a)(i)
blanks.read: PDF downloaded (8.2 MB) and the full extracted text (922,498 characters) grepped for the Russian stem 'zolot'. Note 7 is the strongest near-miss of this slice: the single line of the table reads 'Zoloto na schetakh v inostrannykh bankakh i v slitkakh' (gold on accounts in foreign banks and in bars), 278,261,231 thousand som at 31.12.2024 against 127,413,613 thousand at 31.12.2023, and the note carries a sub-heading 'Kontsentratsiya zolota na depozitakh v inostrannykh bankakh' (concentration of gold on deposits in foreign banks) stating that at both dates the Group held gold on accounts at foreign banks rated A+ by Fitch Ratings Inc., and that balances at those banks exceeded 10 per cent of its own capital. So the document affirms that the monetary gold is at foreign banks and that the exposure is concentrated - and names not one of them. The accounting policy repeats the same unnamed formula in the consolidated and in the separate financial statements (two copies in the one PDF). No custodian name anywhere; also nothing stating any part is held domestically.
blanks.note: Vein for next round: the NBKR discloses rating bands and concentration but not names, consistently across the consolidated and separate statements. The untried route is the NBKR's annual report (a different document from the statements) or its reserve-management regulation, neither of which was opened.

blanks.document: Monetary Authority of Singapore, Financial Statements FY2025/2026, accounting-policy Note 3.9 'Gold'
blanks.read: WEAKER EVIDENCE THAN THE OTHER BLANKS, flagged deliberately. The mas.gov.sg host served an identical 853,817-byte HTML 'Maintenance' page to curl for both the FY2025/26 and the FY2021/22 statements URLs, so no raw PDF text was ever obtained and the file was not greppable. The same URL rendered through WebFetch, which reported that the only gold content is accounting-policy Note 3.9, to the effect that gold is a long-term investment stated at cost with provision for other-than-temporary diminution, that the balance sheet and cash flow statement carry a Gold line (S$5,658 million FY2026, S$7,597 million FY2025) with no note reference, and that nothing in the statements says where the gold is held or who holds it. Because round 74 caught the summariser inventing characterisations, the absence of a location is reported here as a summariser-mediated reading and NOT as a verified full-text grep. Treat as provisional.
blanks.note: Next round: retry the same URL for the raw PDF when mas.gov.sg is out of maintenance, and grep it in full. If it confirms, this becomes a confirmed blank; Singapore's holding is large (MAS bought heavily from 2021) so the note is worth re-reading rather than taking from this summary.
